title: Bosonic quantum computation in PP
formal: Does \[\mathrm{CVBQP}[X^3]\subseteq\mathrm{PP}\] hold for the Gaussian-and-cubic bosonic model below, with no additional restriction on energy during the computation? For every language \(L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*\) decided by the stated polynomial-time uniform bosonic circuit family with polynomial total evolution time and the separated output intervals below, must there be a classical probabilistic polynomial-time machine accepting each \(x\in L\) with probability strictly greater than \(1/2\) and each \(x\notin L\) with probability at most \(1/2\)? The target is the inclusion itself, rather than an unspecified improvement of an exponential-space upper bound.

source_formulation.text: Can the upper bound for bosonic computation with Gaussian and cubic phase gates be improved, in particular to \(\mathrm{CVBQP}[X^3]\subseteq\mathrm{PP}\)?
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase of the source question; the user selected the displayed PP inclusion without an additional energy promise

why: This tests whether an infinite-dimensional optical model with cubic nonlinearity still fits within a familiar classical counting class. Its answer would clarify how much computational power can be hidden in very high intermediate photon numbers despite polynomial evolution time and a bounded-error final decision.
status_note: Source-open. importance.reason: A substantive comparison between infinite-dimensional quantum computation and classical counting complexity, exposing energy and numerical representation as computational resources. The restricted-energy PP theorem makes the distinction from the unrestricted target particularly consequential.

sentences: The selected question asks whether Gaussian-and-cubic bosonic computation is contained in the classical counting class PP.
The model uses coherent input states, polynomial evolution time and a final number measurement with separated acceptance intervals.
No exponential bound on intermediate energy is added to the original formal decision model.
Later PSPACE and PP simulations require additional energy assumptions and therefore do not settle this target.
A resolution would clarify the computational significance of high photon numbers in infinite-dimensional quantum computation.

definitions:
A language is a set of finite binary strings. PP consists of languages for which one classical multitape probabilistic Turing machine, using independent fair random bits, runs in polynomial time on every random tape and has acceptance probability greater than \(1/2\) on exactly the strings in the language. No inverse-polynomial gap from \(1/2\) is required. The machine has no advice or oracle. Its polynomial may depend on the language, but not on the individual input.

For an input of length \(n\ge1\), the bosonic state space is \(L^2(\mathbb R^n)\), the square-integrable complex functions of \(n\) real coordinates. Equivalently it has the orthonormal occupation basis \(|r_1,\ldots,r_n\rangle\) indexed by nonnegative integers. On the usual Schwartz domain, position acts by \((X_j f)(q)=q_jf(q)\), and momentum by \(P_jf=-i\,\partial f/\partial q_j\), with \(i^2=-1\) and units fixed by \([X_j,P_k]=i\delta_{jk}I\). The single-mode number operator is \[N_j=(X_j^2+P_j^2-I)/2,\qquad N_j|r_1,\ldots,r_n\rangle=r_j|r_1,\ldots,r_n\rangle.\] The vacuum is \(|0,\ldots,0\rangle\). These are genuine infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces; there is no finite photon-number cutoff in the model.

For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\{0,1\}^n\), the source's input \(|x\rangle\) means a product of coherent states with real amplitudes \(x_j\), not the occupation state with photon counts \(x_j\). In coordinates its normalized wavefunction is \[\psi_x(q)=\pi^{-n/4}\exp\!\left(-\frac12\sum_{j=1}^n(q_j-\sqrt2x_j)^2\right).\] Preparing this state is the prescribed input convention. Equivalently, input-dependent displacement gates can be placed before a vacuum-input circuit; the displacements have polynomial total cost.

The allowed unitaries are Gaussian gates and single-mode cubic phase gates. A Gaussian gate is \(e^{-itH}\) for a self-adjoint quadratic Hamiltonian \(H\) in the positions and momenta: a real linear combination of \(I,X_j,P_j\) and symmetrized products \((R_aR_b+R_bR_a)/2\), where \(R=(X_1,P_1,\ldots,X_n,P_n)\). A cubic gate is \(e^{-itH}\) with \(H=\pm X_j^3\). Quadratic Hamiltonians and \(\pm X_j^3\) use their standard self-adjoint closures; their exponentials are defined by the spectral calculus. The coefficients of the quadratic Hamiltonians have absolute value bounded by a family-dependent constant. The signs of Hamiltonians may be reversed. Durations are nonnegative; allowing a signed duration is the same convention after moving its sign into the Hamiltonian. Thus total physical evolution time is \(\sum_j|t_j|\), not a signed sum that can cancel. No other non-Gaussian Hamiltonian, intermediate measurement, postselection, feed-forward or non-Gaussian input is allowed.

Uniformity and scalar representation are made explicit as follows. One deterministic classical algorithm on \(1^n\) produces the finite gate list, mode addresses, polynomial lists for the Gaussian Hamiltonians, and the output interval descriptions in polynomial time. The number of listed gates and total description length are polynomial in \(n\). Every real gate parameter is specified by a finite description with one uniform deterministic evaluation algorithm: given \(n\), its location in the list and a unary precision request \(1^b\), the algorithm outputs a dyadic rational within \(2^{-b}\) of that parameter in time polynomial in \(n+b\). Rational parameters and fixed polynomial-time computable constants are included; arbitrary uncomputable real advice is not. These descriptions denote exact real numbers; replacing them by rounded numbers is not a free simulation step. This is the explicit effective-real interpretation of the source's polynomial-time uniformity. In particular, it does not assume that polynomially many precision bits suffice to simulate a circuit whose intermediate energy is very large.

There is a polynomial \(p\), depending only on the family, which bounds the list length, description length, total evolution time and output interval endpoints in magnitude. Write \[|\psi_{n,x}^{\mathrm{out}}\rangle=e^{-it_{\ell(n)}H_{\ell(n)}}\cdots e^{-it_1H_1}|x\rangle.\] At the end, only \(N_1\) is measured. The integer outcome \(Y\in\mathbb N_0\) has probability \[\Pr[Y=r]=\langle\psi_{n,x}^{\mathrm{out}}|\bigl(|r\rangle\langle r|\otimes I\bigr)|\psi_{n,x}^{\mathrm{out}}\rangle.\] Fix polynomial-time computable rational threshold functions \(a(n),b(n),E(n)\), with polynomial-length binary encodings, \(E(n)\ge0\), \(a(n)-E(n)\ge0\), \(b(n)-a(n)\ge1/p(n)\), and all interval endpoints at most \(p(n)\). The family decides \(L\) if, for every input \(x\), \[x\in L\Rightarrow\Pr[Y\in[b(n),b(n)+E(n)]]>2/3,\] \[x\notin L\Rightarrow\Pr[Y\in[a(n)-E(n),a(n)]]>2/3.\] The intervals are inclusive and only their integer points are measurement outcomes. Outcomes outside the indicated interval are part of its error probability. The empty input can be assigned a fixed constant-time decision. All bounds and algorithms are independent of the individual input string.

This is the separated-interval formulation of Definition4.4. Its concentration requirement for the final measurement is retained. It does not itself bound the expectation of that outcome: a small tail at very large photon number can make an expectation large. No promise is added that the total mean energy \(\sum_j\langle N_j\rangle\) remains polynomial or exponential at intermediate times. In particular, no promise of exponentially accurate approximation by exponentially bounded-energy states is imposed. Such a promise is a substantive extra hypothesis in a later PP theorem, not a consequence of the interval acceptance rule.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the inclusion for every language and uniform family in the specified model, or a complete Lean-checked proof that some such language is outside PP. A positive result must cover all allowed polynomial-length Gaussian-and-cubic circuits without adding an intermediate energy or energy-approximation promise. A negative result must establish nonmembership in PP, rather than merely lower bounds for a particular simulation algorithm. The existing EXPSPACE upper bound, a PSPACE upper bound, a PP simulation under extra energy assumptions, or simulation only of low-degree observables does not settle this target. The answer is an exact class-inclusion decision, with no numerical-value approximation tolerance substituted for it.

context_blocks.text: The source asks broadly for a better bound on bosonic computation and explicitly singles out containment in PP. On 16 September2026 the user selected that particular inclusion, with no new energy restriction. This narrows the requested outcome from any improvement of the upper bound to one concrete class comparison; it is not presented as equivalent to the broader objective.

The formal model combines coherent inputs, Gaussian and cubic phase gates, a polynomial total evolution time and a final number measurement with separated acceptance intervals. Its infinite-dimensional state space permits very high occupation numbers during a short computation. The source proves an EXPSPACE upper bound for its Gaussian-and-cubic simulation problem and documents doubly exponential energy growth.

The source uses polynomial final-output energy language in its informal Definition1.2, but its formal Definition4.4 states probability concentration in polynomial-size intervals. Concentration alone does not bound the expectation of a tail. This card explicitly follows the latter formal decision model and does not silently supply a stronger intermediate-energy condition.

The published 2026 PSPACE simulation restricts intermediate energy to at most exponential size. That condition is explicit in the published abstract, introduction and Methods, even though the older arXiv abstract describes a less qualified upper bound. The restricted theorem cannot by itself settle the present inclusion for the original unrestricted-energy model.

The June2026 energy paper goes further and states a PP simulation under an effective exponential-energy approximation promise. Its formal Theorem5.27 also uses constant-bit gate parameters and explicitly says that the promise does not cover the entire Gaussian-and-cubic class. The same paper retains EXPSPACE as the known general simulation bound for polynomial-depth circuits. These qualifications are essential when comparing it with the selected target.

The family here has no adaptive intermediate measurements or additional non-Gaussian input states. Results about richer continuous-variable models, other polynomial Hamiltonians, or expectation values of low-degree observables have different hypotheses or outputs and do not establish this precise inclusion.
